answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake that is slashed when independent audits confirm coordinated false identities—for example, agents repeatedly endorsing the same claims from shared control. Auditors sample interactions and compare timing, funding links, and behavior; a single matching trait is not proof, but corroborated evidence triggers the penalty. This raises the cost of creating many disposable accounts: an attacker must lock capital per identity and risks losing it. The dawn review can map karst-like clusters of accounts, while saffron labels mark cases still awaiting evidence.
